title: A smooth source with locally constant coefficients
statement:
Let $S$ be integral and of finite type over a field $k$, let
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, let $f:X\to S$ be a
separated smooth morphism of
finite type, and let $L$ be a finite locally constant
$\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf. There is a nonempty open $U\subset S$
such that $Rf_{U,*}L|_{X_U}$ is bounded with finite locally
constant cohomology, and for every $v:T\to U$ with Noetherian $T$ the ordinary
base-change morphism

$$
v^*Rf_{U,*}L|_{X_U}\longrightarrow Rf_{T,*}L|_{X_T}
$$

is an isomorphism.
The notation refers to ordinary derived categories.

proof.text: Set $\lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$ and use only the ordinary small etale categories with this constant coefficient ring. The schemes $S$ and $X$ are Noetherian: a field is Noetherian, and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] applies first to $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and then to $X\to S$; finite type also gives quasi-compactness. The dimension function on $X$ is locally constant by [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant] (Stacks Tag 02G1). Its level sets $X_d$ are open and closed. Quasi-compactness gives finitely many nonempty level sets: their open cover has a finite subcover. Each $f_d:X_d\to S$ is separated smooth of finite type of pure relative dimension $d$. Nagata compactification [thm-nagata-compactification] makes it compactifiable. Work on these finitely many pieces and take a common open of $S$ at the end; this is a decomposition of $X$, not of $S$.

Fix one piece and write $f$ for $f_d$. Put $\omega=f^\times\lambda_S$. By [thm-asd-smooth-tensor], $\omega=P[2d]$ with $P$ finite locally constant of rank one. Define $L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_\lambda(L,\lambda_X)$ and $N=L^\vee\otimes_\lambda P[2d]$. This ordinary tensor computes the derived tensor because the sheaves involved are locally finite free. On a trivializing etale neighborhood, $L=\lambda^r$ and $P=\lambda$, so $N=\lambda^r[2d]$ and the evaluation $L\to R\mathcal Hom_\lambda(N,\omega)$ is the bidual map $\lambda^r\to(\lambda^r)^\vee{}^\vee$, in degree zero. The internal Hom functor from $\lambda^r$ is a finite product of the identity and hence exact; there are no higher internal Ext terms. This computes an isomorphism locally, and the sheaf-level geometric-stalk criterion [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to cohomology, checks it globally. It also shows directly that $N$ is bounded constructible in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Internal Hom here is the operation of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the small etale ringed site, not a pro-etale or adic operation.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: construction of N and evaluation

proof.text: Apply [prop-asd-internal-adjunction] with $M=N$ and $K=\lambda_S$. The evaluation identification from the preceding step gives a canonical isomorphism $\alpha_f:Rf_*L\xrightarrow{\sim}D_S(C)$, where $C=Rf_!N$ and $D_S(C)=R\mathcal Hom_\lambda(C,\lambda_S)$. By [lem-fin-compact-bounded-and-base-change], $C$ is bounded constructible. For each nonzero $\mathcal H^q(C)$ choose its finite locally closed stratification from [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The stratum containing the generic point of integral $S$ contains an open neighborhood of that point: write its underlying set as $O\cap Z$, with $O$ open and $Z$ closed; since $Z$ contains the generic point, $Z=S$. Restrict to $O$. The finitely many degrees give a common nonempty open $U$. Include restriction to $U$ in the compact-support base-change clause of [lem-fin-compact-bounded-and-base-change], so that the same construction for $f_U$ has compact direct image $C|_U$. Apply [lem-fin-lisse-field-dual] to $C|_U$. Its cohomology formula makes $D_U(C|_U)$ bounded and finite locally constant, hence so is $Rf_{U,*}L|_{X_U}$ by $\alpha_{f_U}$. No ordinary direct-image finiteness theorem is used.

Let $v:T\to U$ have Noetherian source and let $v_X:X_T\to X_U$ be the other edge. The canonical comparison [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] identifies $v_X^*\omega_{f_U}$ with $\omega_{f_T}$ and respects the tensor map. Pulling back the finite-free evaluation of step 2 identifies $v_X^*N$ with $N_T=(v_X^*L)^\vee\otimes\omega_{f_T}$. This uses the identity $(\lambda^r)^\vee=\lambda^r$ on each trivializing neighborhood; pullback preserves that cover. Put $C_T=Rf_{T,!}N_T$. Compact-support exchange [lem-fin-compact-bounded-and-base-change] gives $b:v^*(C|_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_T$. The canonical dual-pullback map $a:v^*D_U(C|_U)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_T(v^*(C|_U))$ is an isomorphism by [lem-fin-lisse-field-dual]. Thus $D_T(b^{-1})\circ a$, together with $\alpha_{f_U}$ and $\alpha_{f_T}^{-1}$ from [prop-asd-internal-adjunction], gives an isomorphism $\beta:v^*Rf_{U,*}L\to Rf_{T,*}v_X^*L$. The adjunction for $f_T$ is available on its ambient Noetherian category even though $T$ need not be finite type over $k$: the base-changed compactification supplies compactifiability. More explicitly, [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] gives finite type of $f_T$, so [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] and quasi-compactness give Noetherian $X_T$. The chosen compactification base changes to a compactification by [lemma-nagata-compactification-base-change]. The prime $\ell$ stays invertible on $T$ because its inverse in $k$ pulls back along $T\to U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$.

Let $B=Rf_{U,*}L$, let $e:f_U^*B\to L$ be the ordinary counit, and set $H=f_U^*B\otimes^L N$. Evaluation gives $p:H\xrightarrow{e\otimes1}L\otimes^L N\xrightarrow{\mathrm{ev}}\omega_{f_U}$. By [lem-asd-internal-adjunction-evaluation], the tensor transpose of $\alpha_{f_U}$ is $t=\varepsilon_U\circ Rf_{U,!}(p)\circ\Pi_U:B\otimes^L C\to\lambda_U$. Write $b_K:v^*Rf_{U,!}K\to Rf_{T,!}v_X^*K$ for compact exchange, and $c:v_X^*\omega_{f_U}\to\omega_{f_T}$ for the smooth exceptional comparison. These are different maps.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: normalize the internal adjunction by evaluation

proof.text: The complexes $H$ and $\omega_{f_U}$ are bounded constructible: $B$ is bounded lisse by step 3, and locally $N$ and $\omega$ are shifted finite free sheaves by step 2. Thus [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] applies to $p$ and gives $b_{\omega}\circ v^*Rf_{U,!}(p)=Rf_{T,!}(v_X^*p)\circ b_H$. The comparison $c$ of [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] is defined as the exceptional transpose of $v^*\varepsilon_U\circ b_{\omega}^{-1}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to that definition to obtain $\varepsilon_T\circ Rf_{T,!}(c)=v^*\varepsilon_U\circ b_{\omega}^{-1}$. Both sides have source $Rf_{T,!}v_X^*\omega_{f_U}$ and target $\lambda_T$.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: compact exchange naturality and exceptional-counit mate

proof.text:
Put $p_T=c\circ v_X^*p$ and $N'=v_X^*N$, with the identification of step 4. Multiplying the two equations of step 6 cancels $b_{\omega}^{-1}b_{\omega}$ and gives
$$\varepsilon_T Rf_{T,!}(p_T)b_H=v^*(\varepsilon_U Rf_{U,!}(p)).$$
By [lem-asd-compact-projection-exchange],
$$b_Hv^*\Pi_U=\Pi_T(1\otimes b_N),$$
where $\Pi_T:v^*B\otimes^L Rf_{T,!}N'\to Rf_{T,!}(f_T^*v^*B\otimes^L N')$. Hence
$$\varepsilon_T Rf_{T,!}(p_T)\Pi_T(1\otimes b_N)=v^*t.$$
All tensor and inverse-image comparisons in these equations are the canonical ones of the projection-exchange node.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: transport the evaluation pairing through the projection formula

proof.text: The dual pullback comparison $a$ is defined by pulling back evaluation: the tensor transpose of $a\circ v^*\alpha_{f_U}$ is $v^*t$. Precomposing the dual with $b_N^{-1}$, as in step 4, therefore gives tensor transpose $v^*t\circ(1\otimes b_N^{-1})$. The last equation of step 7 identifies it with $\varepsilon_T Rf_{T,!}(p_T)\Pi_T$. By [lem-asd-internal-adjunction-evaluation] over $T$, this is the transpose of the map obtained from $p_T$ by ordinary and tensor--Hom adjunction. Thus that map is the isomorphism $\beta$ of step 4.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: compare the two transposed pairings

proof.text: Under $N'\cong(v_X^*L)^\vee\otimes\omega_{f_T}$, the pairing $p_T$ is the evaluation pairing of $v_X^*e$: pull back $p=\mathrm{ev}\circ(e\otimes1)$ and use the tensor compatibility of [prop-asd-smooth-base-change]. The local finite-free evaluation isomorphism of step 2 therefore identifies its tensor--Hom transpose with $f_T^*v^*B\cong v_X^*f_U^*B\xrightarrow{v_X^*e}v_X^*L$. This is precisely the inverse-image transpose defining ordinary exchange in [sbc-def-base-change-map] on the exchanged square. Equality under the adjunction bijection implies that ordinary exchange equals $\beta$, and hence is an isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, last paragraph: identify the specified ordinary base-change morphism

proof.text: Intersect the nonempty opens obtained for the finitely many $X_d$. They all contain the generic point, so their intersection $U$ is nonempty. A sheaf on a finite disjoint union is the tuple of its restrictions (the sheaf condition on the open-and-closed covering); sections over a base object are the finite product of sections on the pieces. Hence both direct-image constructions and their exchange maps are the finite products of those for $f_d$. Finite products are finite direct sums in an abelian category and are exact, so this equality persists upon deriving. Take the minimum and maximum of the finitely many cohomological bounds. Finite direct sums of finite locally constant sheaves are finite locally constant, as seen on a common trivializing etale cover. The component exchange maps are isomorphisms by step 9; their finite product is an isomorphism. If $X$ is empty the complex is zero and take $U=S$.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: recombination of the dimensions

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $S$ be integral and of finite type over a field $k$, let
$\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, let $f:X\to S$ be a
separated smooth morphism of
finite type, and let $L$ be a finite locally constant
$\mathbf F_\ell$-sheaf. There is a nonempty open $U\subset S$
such that $Rf_{U,*}L|_{X_U}$ is bounded with finite locally
constant cohomology, and for every $v:T\to U$ with Noetherian $T$ the ordinary
base-change morphism

$$
v^*Rf_{U,*}L|_{X_U}\longrightarrow Rf_{T,*}L|_{X_T}
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
Write $\lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$. The relative dimension is
locally constant by
[sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant]; the
finitely many occurring dimensions give a finite disjoint open
decomposition, so we may treat one dimension at a time.
Put $\omega_f=f^\times\lambda_S$. The ambient smooth theorem
[thm-asd-smooth-tensor] says that $\omega_f$ is locally an
invertible sheaf in degree $-2d$, that
$f^\times M=\omega_f\otimes f^*M$. Its compatibility with
Noetherian base change is [prop-asd-smooth-base-change]. In particular
$N=L^\vee\otimes\omega_f$ is bounded constructible and the
finite-dimensional evaluation isomorphism gives

$$
R\mathcal Hom_X(N,\omega_f)=L.
$$

The internal adjunction proved on the ambient categories in
[prop-asd-internal-adjunction] therefore identifies

$$
Rf_*L
=R\mathcal Hom_S(Rf_!N,\lambda_S).
\tag{\(\ast\)}
$$

This invokes neither preservation of a constructible subcategory
by $f^!$ nor ordinary direct-image finiteness.

By [lem-fin-compact-bounded-and-base-change], $C=Rf_!N$
is bounded constructible. Each of its finitely many nonzero
cohomology sheaves is finite locally constant on some nonempty
open of the integral scheme $S$: take the stratum containing
the generic point in the constructible stratification of
[def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], and then its open
neighborhood. Intersect these finitely many opens to obtain $U$.
Apply [lem-fin-lisse-field-dual] to $C|_U$; equation
$(\ast)$ gives the claimed bounded locally constant cohomology.

For $v:T\to U$ with Noetherian $T$, the ambient smooth theorem identifies
$v_X^*N$ with the coefficient complex used for $f_T$.
Compact-support base change identifies
$v^*C$ with $Rf_{T,!}v_X^*N$, and
[lem-fin-lisse-field-dual] permits pullback through its
internal dual. Thus the pullback of $(\ast)$ is the same
isomorphism $(\ast)$ for $f_T$. Naturality of internal
adjunction with respect to its unit and counit identifies this
composite with the ordinary base-change morphism. Hence the
specified morphism, and not merely two abstract objects, is an
isomorphism. Intersect the opens obtained for the finitely many
relative dimensions to finish.
